title: Fleet Sway Controller: regional placement governor with throughput escrow and residency enforcement
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Design and implement a Fleet Sway Controller (FSC) that enforces regional placement policies for dedicated fleets while guaranteeing committed throughput and providing safe failover behavior under zonal outages. FSC coordinates a per-customer throughput escrow, placement hysteresis, and a residency-annotation enforcement layer so contractual residency constraints are respected during scale events and drains. The goal is to enable predictable throughput SLAs for regional pools without risking data-residency violations during emergency failovers.
acceptance_criteria: FSC can assign and enforce a throughput escrow token for a dedicated pool and surface current escrow usage via API and Console
Placement decisions respect customer residency annotations (country/region) and never migrate traffic to non-compliant zones unless an explicit emergency override is triggered
Autoscaler integrates quantile-based target (p95 tail throughput) and honors hysteresis windows to avoid oscillation during bursty traffic
Failover sequence preserves escrow commitments: local soft-siphon first, regional spill/overflow second, cross-region only with an operator-approved emergency flag
End-to-end e2e test harness simulates zone loss and validates routing, billing reconciliation for escrowed units, and audit logs for residency policy decisions
technical_notes: Throughput escrow: allocate 'tokens' (units/sec) per customer pool held by FSC; tokens are deducted on serve and reconciled with billing
Placement governor: scoring function uses locality score, latency quantiles, capacity headroom, and escrow headroom. Apply placement hysteresis (default 90s) to prevent bouncing.
Autoscaler: implement a quantile-based autoscaler (target p95 latency and p50 utilization) with staged probes (soft-scale, hard-scale) and capacity fencing to guarantee escrowed throughput.
Residency enforcement: annotate dedicated nodes with region/country tags; policy engine rejects placements that would violate a customer's residency constraints unless override token provided by SOC
Observability: emit audit events for each placement decision with reason codes (LOCALITY, ESCROW_LOW, CAPACITY_SHORTAGE, OVERRIDE) and link to pool view in Console
rollout_plan: Prototype: scheduler plugin + mock escrow bookkeeping in dev cluster (2 weeks)
Integration: tie FSC to autoscaler agent, placement API, and billing reconciliation service; add audit events to Console (3 weeks)
Canary: pilot with 8 customers across eu-west-1 and us-central-1 to validate throughput SLOs and failover behavior (2 weeks)
Gradual rollout: enable for all new dedicated pools and provide migration tooling for existing commitments (2 weeks)
Operator runbook: document emergency override procedure and rollback steps
risks: Escrow reconciliation drift could cause short-term overstated usage - mitigate with conservative token issuance and hourly reconciliation job
Hysteresis misconfiguration might delay failover - mitigate by staged canary and synthetic zone-loss experiments
Complex policy interactions (geo + partner-affinity) could create ambiguous placement decisions - mitigate with deterministic tie-breaker and explicit Console visibility
Operator overrides can subvert residency guarantees if abused - mitigate with 2-approver workflow and audit trail
qa_steps: Unit tests for escrow allocation, consumption, and reclamation
Integration test: simulate 30s and 5min zone loss; assert no residency violations and escrow commitments honored by failover targets
Load test: drive bursts up to 3x peak to observe hysteresis and autoscale; validate p95 latency remains within SLO for escrowed traffic
Audit trail validation: verify Console shows decision reasons and links to raw event logs
Billing reconciliation test: reconcile escrowed tokens to invoice line items after simulated canary run
